category_title: Students with ASD exhibiting atypical movements and communication difficulties
minimal_context: The student is in an inclusive classroom setting and is being asked to join their peers for a group play activity.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It's time for our group activity. Let's go over to the table and play with the building blocks with your classmates.

STUDENT: (Continues spinning a small plastic wheel on the desk, completely fixated on it and not looking up.)

TUTOR: You can bring the wheel, but we need to go sit with the group now.

STUDENT: (Starts rocking back and forth, getting visibly annoyed) Too loud. Need quiet.

TUTOR: Look, your classmates are trying to get your attention to come play.

STUDENT: (Makes unusual hand movements near their face, staring blankly past the peers who are calling their name, completely ignoring them with a strange expression.)

options.A: Explain to the peers why school discipline and supervision are not applied equally to all pupils, discussing responsibility and blame.
options.B: Provide the student with detailed instruction for each specific element of the group play activity with the building blocks.
options.C: Employ intermittent support for the student while they are participating in the group play activity with the building blocks.
options.D: Use verbal reinforcement for the student when the replacement behavior occurs during the group play activity with the building blocks.
